mainTopic: תקנות of רבן גמליאל הזקן: names in a גט and a widow's vow to collect her כתובה
overview: The amud opens by closing the previous discussion: the הלכה follows נחמני (אביי). A new משנה teaches that a גט was once written only with the names the couple used locally. רבן גמליאל הזקן enacted that it say 'and any name he has / she has,' for תיקון העולם. The גמרא explains that people overseas had asked him what to do when a man is called by different names in different places. רב אשי limits the rule to a man known to have two names, and a ברייתא about a man with two wives in יהודה and גליל proves him right. The חכמי נהרדעא add that the name a woman is mainly called must come first. The next משנה lists more תקנות: a widow collects her כתובה from orphans by making a vow instead of a שבועה, witnesses sign the גט, and הלל enacted the פרוזבול. The גמרא asks why the משנה mentions a widow specifically, and its answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The הלכה follows נחמני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the previous discussion by ruling like נחמני, which is another name for אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like נחמני (אביי).
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the final ruling of the discussion that came just before. The הלכה follows נחמני, meaning אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחמני is a nickname for אביי. In the earlier discussion, the ruling is that when a husband only hints at what he is thinking about the גט (גילוי דעת), it does not count. This line wraps up that topic before the new משנה begins.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a person named נחמני in the new topic. This line belongs to the previous discussion, and נחמני is just אביי.

phrases.english: And the halacha is in accordance with Naḥmani.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the sugya from the previous daf
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows אביי (נחמני) in the previous dispute.

steps.title: The משנה: רבן גמליאל adds 'any other name'
steps.stepSummary: In the past, the גט was written only with the local names of the husband, wife, and their cities. רבן גמליאל הזקן made a תקנה to write 'and any other name he/she has' for תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, the husband would change his name and her name, and the name of his city and her city, to whatever they were called where the גט was written. רבן גמליאל הזקן made a rule that the scribe should write: 'The man so-and-so and any name he has, the woman so-and-so and any name she has.' This was for the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes an old practice for writing names in a גט and a new תקנה from רבן גמליאל הזקן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the old practice, only the names used in the place of writing went into the גט. The risk was that people elsewhere, who knew the couple by different names, would doubt the גט. The תקנה solves this by including every name the person has in one phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: And any name that he has
The betterment of the world, preventing social problems

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of writing all of a person's known names in a גט.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Initially, he would change his name and her name,
phrases.notes: He means changing to the names they were called in the place where the גט was being written.

phrases.english: the name of his city and the name of her city.
Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted
that he should write:
"The man so-and-so, and any name that he has,"
"The woman so-and-so, and any name that she has" –
for the betterment of the world.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט must say 'the man so-and-so and any name he has, the woman so-and-so and any name she has,' because of תיקון העולם.

steps.title: The overseas communities ask about people with two names
steps.stepSummary: שמואל reports that people overseas asked רבן גמליאל how to write a גט for men who are called by one name in one place and another name in another place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The people overseas sent to רבן גמליאל: People who come from there to here, whose name is יוסף but here they call him יוחנן, or whose name is יוחנן but here they call him יוסף, how do they divorce their wives?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the background story behind the משנה's תקנה. This step is the question, and the next step gives רבן גמליאל's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is real: a man is known as יוסף in one place and יוחנן in another. If the גט uses only one name, people in the other place may say it is not his גט. The question sets up why a new rule was needed.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי מְדִינַת הַיָּם לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: The people overseas sent to Rabban Gamliel:
People who come from there to here,
phrases.notes: 'There' is ארץ ישראל and 'here' is the overseas place that sent the question.

phrases.english: his name is Yosef, but they call him Yoḥanan;
or Yoḥanan, but they call him Yosef,
how do they divorce their wives?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי מְדִינַת הַיָּם לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the historical background for the משנה's תקנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to write a valid גט for a man known by different names in different places.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל answers with his תקנה
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל answered by making the תקנה: write 'the man so-and-so and any name he has, the woman so-and-so and any name she has.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל arose and made a rule that they should write: 'The man so-and-so and any name he has, the woman so-and-so and any name she has,' for the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רבן גמליאל's answer to the overseas question. It is the same תקנה we read in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of choosing one name, the גט now covers all of the person's names at once. So wherever the גט is seen, people will recognize it as belonging to this man and woman.
steps.whatToRemember: The תקנה came from a real question: men called by different names in different places. Writing 'and any name he has' covers all of them.

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְהִתְקִין שֶׁיְּהוּ כּוֹתְבִין:
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel arose and instituted that they should write:
"The man so-and-so, and any name that he has,"
"The woman so-and-so, and any name that she has" –
for the betterment of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְהִתְקִין שֶׁיְּהוּ כּוֹתְבִין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Write the main name plus 'and any name he/she has' so the גט covers every name.

steps.title: רב אשי limits the rule to someone known by two names
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says this applies only when the man is actually established as being known by two names.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: And this is only when he is established as having two names.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a limit to the תקנה. It matters only when the person is really known by two names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'and any name he has' covers other names. But רב אשי teaches that you have to deal with a second name only if the man is actually known by it (מוחזק). If he has only one known name, there is no problem to solve.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And this is when he is established with two names.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the scope of רבן גמליאל's תקנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The concern about multiple names applies only when the man is actually known by two names.

steps.title: רבי אבא: other Sages agree with רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא tells רב אשי that רבי מרי and רבי אלעזר hold like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to רב אשי: רבי מרי and רבי אלעזר hold like you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא supports רב אשי by reporting that two other Sages hold the same view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds weight to רב אשי's limit. It is not a new argument. It shows that other Sages already held the same position.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold like you (agree with you)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מָרִי וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר קָיְימִי כְּווֹתָךְ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Mari and Rabbi Elazar hold in accordance with you.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מָרִי וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר קָיְימִי כְּווֹתָךְ
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's limit (only when known by two names)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opinion of רבי מרי and רבי אלעזר, reported by רבי אבא

steps.title: A ברייתא: a man with two wives and two names
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב אשי: a man known by one name in יהודה and another in גליל must write both names in each גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught like רב אשי: If a man had two wives, one in יהודה and one in גליל, and two names, one in יהודה and one in גליל, and he divorced his wife in יהודה with his יהודה name and his wife in גליל with his גליל name, she is not divorced. She is divorced only when he divorces his wife in יהודה with his יהודה name together with the גליל name, and his wife in גליל with his גליל name together with the יהודה name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רב אשי. A man known by two names in two places must include both names in the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This man is clearly established with two names, one in each region. That is exactly רב אשי's case, so one name alone does not work. Both names must appear in each גט.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a בָּרַיְיתָא in support of him

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rav Ashi:
If he had two wives –
one in Judea and one in the Galilee;
and he has two names –
one in Judea and one in the Galilee;

phrases.aramaic: וְגֵרַשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁבִּיהוּדָה בִּשְׁמוֹ שֶׁבִּיהוּדָה,
phrases.english: and he divorced his wife in Judea with his Judea name,
and his wife in the Galilee with his Galilee name –
she is not divorced,
phrases.notes: This applies to each of the two wives. Neither one is divorced.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּגָרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁבִּיהוּדָה בִּשְׁמוֹ שֶׁבִּיהוּדָה –
phrases.english: until he divorces his wife in Judea with his Judea name –
with the Galilee name along with it;
and his wife in the Galilee with his Galilee name –
with the Judea name along with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Further support for רב אשי, this time from a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's rule that both names are needed when a man is known by two names
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a man with two wives and two names in יהודה and גליל

steps.title: If he moved elsewhere, one name is enough
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: if the man went to a different place and divorced with only one of the names, the divorce is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he went out to a different place and divorced with one of them, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with an exception. In a new place, one name alone is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new place he is not known there by two names. So רב אשי's condition, being established with two names, does not apply. This is exactly why the ברייתא supports רב אשי: the need for both names depends on actually being known by both.

keyTerms.meaning: He went out to a different place

steps.whatToRemember: Two names are needed in the גט only where the man is actually known by two names. Where he is not known that way, one name works. That is רב אשי's rule, and the ברייתא backs it up.

phrases.english: If he went out to a different place,
and divorced with one of them –
phrases.notes: 'One of them' means one of his two names.

phrases.english: she is divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצָא לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר, וְגֵרַשׁ בְּאֶחָד מֵהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the same ברייתא, giving the exception
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a place where he is not known by both names, a גט with one of his names is valid.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא seems to contradict its beginning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the end of the ברייתא can allow one name, when its beginning required the גליל name to be added even in יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say that the name he uses in the גליל must be written with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction inside the ברייתא. The beginning says to write both names, but the end says one name is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא said that even in יהודה you must add the name he is called in the גליל. The last part said that if he went elsewhere and divorced with only one name, the גט is valid. So it looks like the ברייתא both requires both names and does not require them.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you say? (introduces a contradiction with something already stated)
The name he is called in the גליל
With it, written alongside the other name

phrases.english: But didn't you say that the name of the Galilee must be with it!
phrases.notes: This points back to the first half of the same ברייתא from step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ending of the ברייתא (step 8) by contrasting it with the ברייתא's opening ruling (step 7).
steps.kashyaTarget: The final clause of the ברייתא, which allows a גט with only one name
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The opening clause demands both names even in יהודה, so it seems impossible for the closing clause to accept a single name.

steps.title: Two different cases: known to have two names versus not known
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. The beginning of the ברייתא is about a man established as having two names, and the end is about a man who is not established that way. This confirms רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from it: this case is where he is established as having two names, and this case is where he is not established. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two halves of the ברייתא are talking about different situations. It concludes that this proves רב אשי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where people know he has two names, both must be written. When he goes to a place where nobody knows his second name, one name is enough. This is exactly what רב אשי said in step 5: the rule of writing all names applies only when the man is known by two names.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; conclude from this
Where it is established (that he has two names)

steps.whatToRemember: You only need to write a second name in a גט when it is known that the person has two names (רב אשי). In יהודה he is not called by his גליל name, but people there know he has it, so it must be added. In a new place where nobody knows he has two names, one name is enough.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it –
this is where he is established,
phrases.notes: Meaning people there know he goes by two names. That is the first half of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: this is where he is not established;
learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 9 and closes the proof for רב אשי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: each half of the ברייתא refers to a different situation (known by two names versus not known)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say both that both names are required and that one name is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both names are required only where he is established as having both. Where he is not, one name works. This proves רב אשי.

steps.title: A woman mostly called מרים and sometimes שרה
steps.stepSummary: For a woman most people called מרים and a few called שרה, the חכמי נהרדעא rule that the גט says 'מרים and any name she has,' not 'שרה and any name she has.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a woman whom people called מרים, and a few called her שרה. The Sages of נהרדעא said: write 'מרים and any name she has,' and not 'שרה and any name she has.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case about names in a גט and gives the ruling of the חכמי נהרדעא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when using רבן גמליאל's formula of 'and any name she has,' the main written name must be the one most people use. Her minor name cannot lead, even with the 'any name' phrase added.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain (woman); opens a story of an actual case
The Sages of the city נהרדעא
Any name that she has (רבן גמליאל's formula)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the phrase 'and any name she has' makes the order unimportant. The main name she is known by must come first.

phrases.english: A certain woman whom they would call Miriam,
and a few called her Sara.
The Sages of Neharde'a said:
Write "Miriam and any name that she has,"

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שָׂרָה וְכֹל שׁוּם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ.
phrases.english: and not "Sara and any name that she has."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבן גמליאל's 'any name' formula to a practical case and adds a detail about which name must lead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a גט, the name a person is mainly known by is written first, followed by 'and any name she has.'

steps.title: New משנה: a widow collects her כתובה with a vow
steps.stepSummary: A widow may collect from orphans' property only with a שבועה. When courts stopped giving her the oath, רבן גמליאל הזקן enacted that she make any vow the orphans want and then collect her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow cannot collect from the property of orphans except with an oath. They held back from making her swear. רבן גמליאל הזקן enacted that she makes a vow to the orphans, whatever they want, and collects her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, continuing the list of תקנות. It describes how a widow can collect her כתובה from her late husband's orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is that she must swear before collecting from the orphans. When courts stopped giving her that oath, she was left unable to collect. רבן גמליאל הזקן replaced the oath with a vow of the orphans' choosing, so she can still collect.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה

steps.confusionAlert: A נדר (vow) is not the same as a שבועה (oath). The תקנה swaps the oath for a vow.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A widow does not collect from the property of orphans,
except with an oath.
They refrained from making her swear;
phrases.notes: "They" means the courts. The משנה doesn't say why here.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted,
that she should vow for the orphans
whatever they wish,
and she collects her marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין אַלְמָנָה נִפְרַעַת מִנִּכְסֵי יְתוֹמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, moving from the names in a גט to another תקנה of רבן גמליאל הזקן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow collects her כתובה from orphans by making whatever vow they request, in place of the oath.

steps.title: Witnesses sign the גט, and הלל's פרוזבול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists two more תקנות made for תיקון העולם: witnesses sign on the גט, and הלל enacted the פרוזבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The witnesses sign on the גט, for the betterment of the world. And הלל enacted the פרוזבול, for the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of rabbinic enactments made for תיקון העולם. The גמרא will explain each one later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate enactments are listed. The first is that witnesses put their signatures on the גט. The second is הלל's פרוזבול, a document that keeps שמיטה from cancelling a debt. The משנה gives only the label 'for the betterment of the world' and leaves the reasons for the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: The betterment of the world; the reason behind these תקנות
A document that keeps שמיטה from cancelling a debt

steps.whyThisMatters: These lines continue the theme of the whole פרק: rabbinic enactments made for תיקון העולם.

phrases.english: The witnesses sign on the bill of divorce,
for the betterment of the world.
And Hillel instituted the prosbul,
for the betterment of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָעֵדִים חוֹתְמִין עַל הַגֵּט מִפְּנֵי תִּיקּוּן הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה's list of enactments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses sign on a גט, and הלל enacted the פרוזבול, both for תיקון העולם.

steps.title: Why mention a widow specifically?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה limits the oath rule to an אלמנה, since anyone collecting from orphans needs a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה talk only about a widow? This applies to everyone, because we already know that anyone collecting from orphans' property can collect only with an oath!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking why the widow is singled out. The oath rule seems to be a general rule, not a widow rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said an אלמנה collects from the orphans only with a שבועה. But there is a known general rule that anyone collecting from יתומים needs an oath. So mentioning the widow looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? (asks why the text picked one example)
We hold as an established rule

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why specifically a widow?
The same is true for everyone!
For we hold as an established rule:
one who comes to collect from the property of orphans
may collect only with an oath!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא אַלְמָנָה, אֲפִילּוּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's widow rule from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice to mention an אלמנה specifically.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general rule already requires a שבועה from anyone collecting from orphans, so the widow detail seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The widow case was needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the widow case had to be stated, and begins to explain what we would otherwise have thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: The widow case was necessary, because you might have thought:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer by saying the משנה needed to mention the widow. This line sets up the next move, where the גמרא explains what mistaken idea we might have had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not deny the general rule. It says there was a special reason to think a widow might be different, so the משנה had to spell it out. The actual reason continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to teach it)
It would enter your mind to say (introduces a mistaken first thought)

phrases.english: It was necessary for him to teach the case of a widow,
since it would have entered your mind to say:
